claim: Quantpedia's 'Momentum Factor Effect in Country Equity Indexes' (source paper Muller & Ward 2010, Studies in Economics and Econometrics 34(1)): rank ~70 MSCI World country equity indexes by 10-12 month momentum, hold the top 4-5 for one month, monthly rebalance. Reported backtest 1970-2009 (Muller & Ward's own sample): the 4-best-of-70 portfolio outperformed an equal-weighted benchmark by ~10%/yr; Quantpedia's own figure-13 readout at Quantpedia's chosen parameters: 17.7%/yr, max drawdown -65.39%, Sharpe not disclosed. Quantpedia's page cites a 2024 update (Du & Jiang) noting the efficacy of ETF momentum strategies 'while robust until around 2010, began to show signs of waning in subsequent years.'
quote: a strategy of holding for one month, a portfolio of the four best performing MSCI country indices over the previous 11 months, was found to persistently out-perform an equal weighted benchmark by around 10% per annum.
limitations: Practitioner summary page (not the original 2010 journal paper text); the 1970-2009 sample and the page's own 17.7%/yr figure are long-only-4-of-70-country readouts at Quantpedia's own chosen lookback, pre-2010, and the page itself cites a 2024 note that the effect 'began to show signs of waning' after ~2010 -- used only for the cross-sectional-momentum-across-country-equities mechanism, never for these sample numbers, which is why K1/K2 are tested fresh in this batch.
independent_replication: No independent third-party live/forward record of a long-only, absolute-momentum-filtered, US-listed single-country-ETF rotation was found in this or a prior gap-search round.
impact_on_spec: Grounds the COUNTRY menu's mechanism (cross-sectional momentum across country equities); this batch tests the already-validated rotation_cell/make_rotation_fn mechanism on this menu against K1/K2, not Quantpedia's own 1970-2009 or figure-13 numbers.
